chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought goods and they became un-saleable upon him, and he had already paid Zakat on his wealth before buying the goods. When should he pay Zakat? He (peace be upon him) said: If he withheld his goods seeking to recover his capital wealth, then there is no Zakat upon it; and if he withheld it after he had recovered the capital of his wealth, then upon him is the Zakat after he had withheld it after (the recovery) of the capital wealth.
He (the narrator) said, And I asked him about the man who has deposits of wealth with him to work with these. So he (peace be upon him) said: When the year passes by, let him pay Zakat on it.

key_terms.حَال الْحَوْل: When the year passes (lunar year for Zakat)

ai.seo_question: When is Zakat due on unsaleable commercial goods in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the timing of Zakat liability on commercial goods by distinguishing between goods held to recover initial capital, which are exempt until that capital is realized, and those held for profit after capital recovery, which incur Zakat upon the completion of the lunar year. This ruling establishes a practical framework for merchants, ensuring that Zakat is levied on actual wealth accumulation rather than mere possession, while also confirming that deposited capital for trade is subject to the same annual cycle. The distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential focus on the economic reality of the asset's status at the time of Zakat calculation.
